# Semantic ownership acceptance fixtures (specification)

This is a **test specification**, not an implemented ownership graph or a passing automated test. Do not enable semantic writes based on this document.

## Required synthetic ROM cases

1. Two disjoint adjacent fixed tables: both remain readable, no false collision.
2. Nested child table inside a parent record: report unresolved ownership until upstream parent/child semantics are implemented; do not claim both as independent writable owners.
3. One complete pointer field with an identical `OffsetPointer` declaration: allow read-only overlay; reject mismatched displacement.
4. Pointer spanning a table-row boundary: suppress typed interpretation.
5. Two partially overlapping `MatchedWords` sources: suppress all dependent typed lengths, even if decoded values happen to agree.
6. Parent length derived from a conflicted constant: suppress parent and all transitive dependents.
7. Edited staged ROM changing a count: recompute read-only spans and conflicts after edit, undo and redo; do not mutate the source ROM.
8. ROM expansion beyond supported pointer encoding: refuse relocation and do not emit an apparently valid pointer.
9. Ambiguous stock/custom metadata overlays: preserve both declarations, mark conflict and block semantic writes.
10. Unknown dynamic format or nested run: report unsupported, not free space.

## Release gate

Implement each fixture as an executable regression in `tests/`, using only generated bytes and redistributable metadata. Verify against pinned upstream CUBHMA behavior, add ROM checksum and unchanged-input assertions, and run CI plus Android device tests. Until then, the ownership engine is read-only and incomplete.
